chunks: Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

Regarding a man who marries into a family, and his wife is 'awra' (has a defect) and they did not specify it to him, he said: The marriage is not annulled; rather, the marriage is annulled due to leprosy, leprosy (specific type), madness, and blindness. I said: Do you see if he has consummated the marriage with her, what should he do regarding her dowry? He said: She has the dowry because he made her private part permissible to him, and her guardian who married her off must pay a penalty equal to what he brought to her.

key_terms.عَوْرَاءُ: Having a defect or physical flaw

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on marriage annulment and dowry when a wife has an undisclosed defect?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *al-Istibsar* to clarify that specific physical defects like leprosy (*baras*) and madness (*junun*) are grounds for annulment, whereas other hidden defects (*'awab*) do not automatically void the marriage contract. If consummation has occurred, the wife retains her full dowry (*mahr*) as compensation for her right to be intimate, while the husband seeks reimbursement from the guardian who concealed the defect, reflecting the Shia principle of fairness in marital transactions.
